message.content:
Internal survey for a new flagship product called **NxLabs** being added to Nxeon (/opt/nxeon), a VPS + game-server hosting platform. NxLabs is a catalog of mods / plugins / shaders / texture packs / world saves for the ~47 game families Nxeon hosts, with: public SEO-optimised marketing pages (one per mod, with images), a customer-portal browser with "Add to my server" one-click install, an admin management console, reviews/comments, and a community creator-submission program.

This is READ-ONLY research — do NOT write or modify any code. I need to know exactly what already exists that this should build on, and where it plugs in.

## What to investigate and report (with file paths + line numbers)

**1. Storage capacity — where can we actually put mod files?**
The owner explicitly asked to "find some space on a node drive." Survey the real disks across all nodes. You can SSH to the Proxmox hosts as root (this works, key-based): primary `51.79.162.96`, node-2 `178.63.94.114`, node-3 `15.235.145.177`, node-4 `139.99.125.21`. Run read-only `df -h`, `zfs list`, `pvesm status` on each. Report free space per node per storage pool, and recommend where a growing mod mirror (potentially hundreds of GB) should live and why. Note: node-3 is known to be memory-constrained and oversold; node-4 is mostly empty. Also check whether there's any existing object-storage/CDN/S3 integration in the codebase already (grep for S3, Backblaze, R2, minio, bunny, cloudflare) that might be a better home than a node disk.

**2. Existing schema patterns.** Read `prisma/schema.prisma` and report the conventions this codebase uses that a new NxLabs schema should match: id strategy (cuid?), timestamps, soft-delete vs hard-delete patterns, enum style, how `Server`/`GamePlan`/`User` relate, how existing "catalog" style tables (`OsTemplate`, `GamePlan`, `Coupon`) are shaped and seeded. Also: is there ANY existing table remotely related to mods/plugins/content? (grep for mod, plugin, addon, workshop.)

**3. Game-server file access + install mechanics — how would "Add to my server" actually work?**
This is the critical integration. Report how the platform currently manipulates files inside a customer's game server:
- `lib/sftp.ts` (SFTP helpers: `withSftp`, `writeFileBuffer`, `mkdirPath`, etc.) and `lib/ssh-exec.ts` (`withServerSsh`, `exec`).
- How game servers are structured: `worker/index.ts`'s `wrapDockerGameService`, the per-family docker containers, and where game data lives on disk inside the guest (e.g. Minecraft's data dir, the bind-mount convention — I know Bedrock uses `/opt/bedrock:/data`).
- `lib/game-control.ts` (`controlSpec`, serviceHints) — how start/stop/restart works per family, since installing a mod needs a restart.
- Is there an existing in-portal **file manager** (the SFTP proxy suggests yes) and an existing job type that writes files to a server? List the relevant `Job` types in the schema/worker.
- Where would a mod actually need to be placed per family? Report what you can determine for at least: Minecraft Java (mods/ vs plugins/ depending on loader), Minecraft Bedrock (behavior_packs/resource_packs + world JSON manifests — note the `upnormal` server is a live real example), Valheim, Rust, Factorio.

**4. Admin portal conventions.** The owner wants admin management of the mod DB, including marking items "no longer supported". Report how `app/admin/` is structured: routing, the shared table/list UI components, how existing admin CRUD works (e.g. `/admin/nodes` recently got an editable field — look at `components/admin/NodeForms.tsx` and `lib/actions-nodes.ts` as the current best-practice example), the `requireAdmin` + `audit()` + `revalidatePath` action pattern, and how admin settings panels are built (`lib/actions-settings.ts`, `components/admin/settings/`).

**5. Marketing SEO page infrastructure.** NxLabs needs potentially thousands of individual mod pages. Report on the proven dynamic-page pattern: `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` + `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` + `UseCaseLanding` (this reportedly serves 100+ pages from one route with automatic sitemap inclusion via `app/sitemap.ts`). Explain exactly how a new large page family would hook into `generateStaticParams` and the sitemap. Also report what JSON-LD/structured-data helpers exist (`FaqJsonLd`, `ProductOffersJsonLd`, etc.) since mod pages want Product/SoftwareApplication + AggregateRating schema.

**6. Reviews / comments / user-generated content.** Does ANYTHING like this exist already (reviews, ratings, comments, moderation)? grep for review, rating, comment, testimonial. The homepage shows Trustpilot-style review badges — are those real records or static marketing copy? Also: is there an existing image-upload/asset-storage path for user-submitted content (for the creator program), and any existing moderation tooling?

**7. Customer portal conventions.** How is `app/dashboard/` structured, how does the game panel work (`components/customer/gamepanel/`), and where would a "Mods" tab most naturally live for a game server? Check `lib/nx/nav.ts` (reportedly the authoritative nav registry) for how a new section gets registered.

Be concrete and cite file paths + line numbers. Where something genuinely doesn't exist yet, say so plainly — that's just as useful. Do not speculate about code you haven't read.

- artifact-capabilities: Runtime capabilities a published Artifact page can be granted — behavior static HTML cannot provide on its own, such as the page reading live or connected data, remembering what people do on it (a poll, a sign-up sheet, a checklist, a document edited in place — it saves new versions of itself), keeping state shared across viewers, knowing who is viewing, asking Claude a question of its own, storing files people add, or handing the viewer a file to save. Serves this user's live capability roster and the typed call definitions. Load it whenever any such runtime behavior would make an artifact more useful, before writing the page.
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.
- fewer-permission-prompts: Scan your transcripts for common read-only Bash and MCP tool calls, then add a prioritized allowlist to project .claude/settings.json to reduce permission prompts.
- loop: Run a prompt or slash command on a recurring interval (e.g. /loop 5m /foo). Omit the interval to let the model self-pace. - When the user wants to set up a recurring task, poll for status, or run something repeatedly on an interval (e.g. "check the deploy every 5 minutes", "keep running /babysit-prs"). Do NOT invoke for one-off tasks.
- schedule: Create, update, list, or run scheduled cloud agents (routines) that execute on a cron schedule. - When the user wants to schedule a recurring cloud agent, set up automated tasks, create a cron job for Claude Code, or manage their scheduled agents/routines. READ-ONLY research in /opt/nxeon (Next.js App Router + Prisma). Do NOT modify any file. Report with absolute file paths + line numbers. Be concrete; if something doesn't exist, say so plainly.

TOPIC A — Admin portal conventions:
1. Structure of /opt/nxeon/app/admin/ — routing layout, how many sections, the layout.tsx / nav registry for admin.
2. Read /opt/nxeon/components/admin/NodeForms.tsx and /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-nodes.ts fully — describe the current best-practice CRUD pattern (server action signature, FormData vs typed args, requireAdmin, audit(), revalidatePath, error return shape, toast/pending UI in the client component).
3. Shared admin table/list UI components — find them (likely /opt/nxeon/components/admin/*, maybe a DataTable / AdminTable / Card / ui primitives). List the reusable ones a new admin CRUD console should use.
4. Admin settings panels: read /opt/nxeon/lib/actions-settings.ts and /opt/nxeon/components/admin/settings/ — how a settings panel + feature flag is defined and persisted (what table backs settings?).
5. How does requireAdmin work, and where is audit() defined (file + signature)?

TOPIC B — Marketing SEO page infrastructure:

1	/**
2	 * Whether a catalogue entry can actually be installed with one click.
3	 *
4	 * WHY THIS IS ITS OWN MODULE. Two independent things have to both be true, and
5	 * until now neither was checked before the button was drawn:
6	 *
7	 *   1. the worker knows WHERE this game keeps its mods
8	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `modDirShell`), and
9	 *   2. the worker can turn this entry's source into a DOWNLOAD URL
10	 *      (worker/game-mods.ts's `resolveUrl`).
11	 *
12	 * The catalogue is far wider than either. Expanding it from 124 entries across
13	 * five games to 491 across eight made that gap much bigger rather than smaller:
14	 * every Factorio, Satisfactory, Palworld, CS2 and V Rising entry got an Install
15	 * button that reaches the worker and comes back "Auto-install isn't wired for
16	 * this game yet." A button whose only outcome is an error is worse than no
17	 * button, and it is worse again at 178 of them.
18	 *
19	 * So the two lists live here, `worker/game-mods.ts` imports them rather than
20	 * keeping its own copies, and the panel asks the same question before it
21	 * decides what to render. One source of truth, so the UI and the worker cannot
22	 * disagree about what is possible.
23	 *
24	 * ADDING A FAMILY is deliberately a two-part job: add its directory to
25	 * `modDirShell` AND its slug here. Adding it here alone re-creates exactly the
26	 * failure this module exists to prevent.
27	 */
28	
29	/** Families whose mod directory `worker/game-mods.ts` knows how to find. */
30	export const INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES = new Set(["minecraft", "rust", "valheim"]);
31	
32	/** Sources `worker/game-mods.ts` can resolve to a downloadable file. */
33	export const RESOLVABLE_SOURCES = new Set(["modrinth", "spigotmc", "umod", "thunderstore"]);
34	
35	export type InstallSupport =
36	  | { ok: true }
37	  | { ok: false; reason: "family" | "source"; message: string };
38	
39	/**
40	 * Can this entry be installed for the customer, or does it have to be done by
41	 * hand? The message is customer-facing and says which of the two is missing,
42	 * because they lead to different next steps: a family we can't reach means
43	 * upload it yourself, a source we can't fetch from means download it first.
44	 */
45	export function installSupport(family: string, source: string): InstallSupport {
46	  if (!INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES.has(family)) {
47	    return {
48	      ok: false,
49	      reason: "family",
50	      message: "We can't place files for this game automatically yet — install it yourself in Files.",
51	    };
52	  }
53	  if (!RESOLVABLE_SOURCES.has(source)) {
54	    return {
55	      ok: false,
56	      reason: "source",
57	      message: "This source doesn't offer a direct download we can fetch — grab the file and upload it in Files.",
58	    };
59	  }
60	  return { ok: true };
61	}

 * slugs and rendered copy are clean. Unknown extra fields are ignored by upsertPost.
 *
 * Run: cd /opt/nxeon && node scripts/seo-mods.mjs   (idempotent, upsert by slug)

/** Decode the handful of HTML entities the agents emitted. & is decoded LAST
 *  so a double-encoded "&lt;" resolves to "<" not "<". */
function decode(s) {
  if (typeof s !== "string") return s;
  return s
    .replace(/</g, "<")
    .replace(/>/g, ">")
    .replace(/"/g, '"')
    .replace(/&#0?39;/g, "'")
    .replace(/'/gi, "'")
    .replace(///gi, "/")
    .replace(/'/g, "'")
    .replace(/&/g, "&");
}

function decodePost(p) {
  const out = { ...p };
  for (const k of ["title", "excerpt", "seoTitle", "seoDescription", "body"]) {

206	  if (!re) return setupScript;

208	  const matchIndex = setupScript.indexOf(full);
209	  if (matchIndex < 0) return setupScript;

211	  // Strip docker's own restart policy — systemd now owns restart semantics for
212	  // this container, and leaving both in place makes the two supervisors fight
213	  // over a crash-looping process.
214	  const cleanedAfter = after.replace(/\s*--restart(?:=|\s+)\S+/, "");
215	  // Cap the container's json-file log driver. No game image's setupScript ever
216	  // set this, so a crash-looping container (systemd restarting it every 5s
217	  // forever — see RestartSec above) grows an unbounded log file. Root-caused
218	  // live 2026-09-17 on projectzomboid-kc0kcr: its docker json log alone had
219	  // grown to ~28 GB (on top of ~28.5 GB of rsyslog spamming its own
220	  // "no space left on device" write failures once the disk filled), filling
221	  // the 77 GB root disk to 100% and taking the game server down. This is the
222	  // single construction point every game family's `docker run` is rewritten
223	  // through, so applying the cap here covers all of them at once rather than
224	  // editing each family's setupScript individually. 10m x 3 files = a 30 MB
225	  // ceiling per container regardless of how long or how hard it crash-loops.
226	  const createCmd = `docker create --name ${containerName} --log-opt max-size=10m --log-opt max-file=3${before}${cleanedAfter}`

235	    "After=docker.service",
236	    "Requires=docker.service",
237	    "",

### B7. `/opt/nxeon/lib/nx/nav.ts` (117 lines) — the nav registry

```ts
type NavItem = { group: string; label: string; icon: string; href: string; badge?: string };
```

A **flat array** `NAV: NavItem[]` at `:17-72`; grouping is derived from the `group` string, not nested. Groups in order of first appearance: `Overview`, `Compute`, `Build`, `Tools`, `Network`, `Mail`, `Account`.

## A5. `requireAdmin` and `audit()`

**`requireAdmin`** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts:229-233`:
```ts
export async function requireAdmin(): Promise<User> {
  const user = await requireUser();
  if (user.role !== "ADMIN") throw new Error("FORBIDDEN");
  return user;
}
```
It builds on `requireUser()` (`auth.ts:223-227`, throws `"UNAUTHORIZED"`), which uses `currentUser()` — i.e. **impersonation-aware**. Related guards in the same file: `requireStaff()` `:240` (uses `realUser()`, ignores impersonation), `assertNotImpersonating()` `:212`, `impersonating()`, `realUser()`.

For **page-level** guards the convention is `requireArea(area)` from `/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:174-180`, which **redirects** (`/login`, `/dashboard`, `/admin`) rather than throwing. `Area` union `rbac.ts:14-38`; `AREA_ROLES` `:40`; `canAccess` `:63`; `isStaff` `:67`; `HREF_AREA` map `:72-159`; `areaForHref` `:161`; `canAccessHref` `:165`.

**`audit()` — there is no single `audit()` export. There are two things:**

1. **The shared writer: `recordAudit(userId: string | null, action: string, detail?: string): Promise<void>`** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/audit.ts:15-22`. It additionally resolves `impersonating()` and appends `actingAdmin=<id>` to `detail` so actions taken during impersonation are attributed to the real admin (`:18-20`). Its own doc comment (`:4-14`) states it was extracted from a private `audit()` in `lib/actions.ts` and that "every other `lib/actions-*.ts` module wrote `db.auditLog.create(...)` ad hoc".

2. **Eight per-file private copies** named `audit()`, all with the same body but **without** the impersonation attribution:
   - `lib/actions-nodes.ts:29`, `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:19`, `lib/actions-billing.ts:8`, `lib/actions-improvements.ts:25`, `lib/actions-staging.ts:14`, `lib/actions-accounting.ts:26`, `lib/actions-work.ts:33`, `lib/actions-company-mail.ts:78`.

   Plus 66 files in `lib/` that call `db.auditLog.create` directly.

For a **new** admin CRUD console, import `recordAudit` from `@/lib/audit` — that is the intended target, even though `actions-nodes.ts` (the reference implementation you asked about) predates it and uses its own copy.

**`AuditLog` model** — `prisma/schema.prisma:1099+`: `{ id, userId?, action, detail?, createdAt, ip?, category? }`. Note `ip` and `category` exist but neither `recordAudit` nor the local `audit()` helpers populate them.

## B7. `app/sitemap.ts` — hooking in a new large family

`/opt/nxeon/app/sitemap.ts` (279 lines). Single `MetadataRoute.Sitemap` at `/sitemap.xml`. `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` `:9`. `APP_URL` `:7`.

**Structure:**
1. `staticRoutes` array of `{path, priority, freq}` `:14-173` — ~130 hand-listed entries, mapped to entries at `:175-180`.
2. Programmatic families, each an explicit `for` loop pushing entries:
   - `LANDING_SLUGS` → priority 0.7 `:183-190`
   - `REGION_LANDING_SLUGS` → 0.75 `:196-203`
   - `GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS` → 0.6 `:209-216`
   - `GENERAL_LOCATION_SLUGS` → 0.7 `:222-229`
3. DB-driven families, each wrapped in `try/catch` so a missing model can't break the sitemap:
   - Blog posts `:232-251` (defensively feature-detects `db.blogPost` at `:233`)
   - `db.freeMinecraftServer` public+READY → `/servers/{subdomain}` `:260-276`

**How a new "thousands of mod pages" family hooks in:**
1. Export a `MOD_PAGE_SLUGS: string[]` (or an async loader) from a new `lib/marketing/*.ts`.
2. `import` it at the top of `app/sitemap.ts` alongside `:4-5`.
3. Add one `for (const slug of MOD_PAGE_SLUGS) entries.push({ url: \`${APP_URL}/${slug}\`, lastModified: now, changeFrequency: "monthly", priority: 0.5 })` block after `:229`.
4. If slugs come from the DB (`GameMod` rows), copy the `try/catch` idiom at `:260-276` rather than the bare loops.

**Size limits — this is the real risk, and nothing in the repo handles it:**
- **There is no sitemap index.** No `generateSitemaps()` export anywhere, no `app/sitemap/[id]/` route, no `sitemap-index.xml`. `/opt/nxeon/app/robots.ts:18` hardcodes a single `sitemap: ${APP_URL}/sitemap.xml`.
- Current entry count is roughly **130 static + 765 programmatic + blog + public free-MC servers ≈ 900-1000+**, comfortably under the 50,000-URL / 50 MB uncompressed sitemap protocol limit.
- Adding "thousands of mod pages" stays under 50,000 unless the family is very large. `GameMod` is keyed `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` (`prisma/schema.prisma:2932`) with 41 active families — a per-family × per-mod cross-product could plausibly blow past it.
- Because the route is `force-dynamic`, every `/sitemap.xml` request re-runs the whole builder **plus** the two DB queries. At tens of thousands of entries that becomes a real per-request cost with no caching in front of it.
- If you exceed ~10-25k entries, the Next.js-idiomatic fix is `export function generateSitemaps()` in `app/sitemap.ts`, which emits `/sitemap/0.xml`, `/sitemap/1.xml`, … and requires updating `app/robots.ts:18`. **That work does not exist yet.**

## B9. Marketing images

**`next/image` config: there is none.** `/opt/nxeon/next.config.ts` has **no `images` key at all** — no `remotePatterns`, no `domains`, no `formats`, no `deviceSizes`. A new page family that needs remote images (e.g. Modrinth/CurseForge icon CDNs, `GameMod.iconUrl` at `prisma/schema.prisma:2896`) **will fail** with `next/image` until `images.remotePatterns` is added.

**`next/image` is barely used in marketing** — only 4 files: `components/marketing/ClaudeMark.tsx`, `components/marketing/CompetitorLogo.tsx`, `components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx`, `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx`.

**`public/` conventions:**

```
  games/art/       127 files — <game>_hero.jpg, <game>_logo.png, <game>_poster.jpg
```

## A2. Best-practice CRUD pattern — `lib/actions-nodes.ts` + `components/admin/NodeForms.tsx`

**Server action signatures — two distinct shapes, used deliberately:**

1. **Form actions (FormData)** — for the add/edit form, consumed by `useActionState`:
   - `addNode(_prev: FormState, formData: FormData): Promise<FormState>` — `actions-nodes.ts:169`
   - `updateNode(_prev: FormState, formData: FormData): Promise<FormState>` — `actions-nodes.ts:195`
2. **Typed-arg actions** — for inline row controls, consumed by `useTransition`:
   - `setNodeEnabled(id: string, enabled: boolean)` — `:229`
   - `setNodeAcceptsProvisions(id, acceptsProvisions)` — `:246`
   - `setNodeStatus(id, status: NodeStatus)` — `:258`
   - `setNodeMonthlyCost(id, rawDollars: string)` — `:278` (raw dollar string on the wire, cents in the DB)
   - `testNode(id): Promise<TestNodeResult>` — `:330`
   - `deleteNode(id)` — `:381`
   - `suggestNodeDefaults(): Promise<NodeDefaults>` — `:38` (server-computed non-colliding defaults for a new row)

**Error return shape.** `type FormState = { error?: string; ok?: boolean }` — `actions-nodes.ts:27`. Every action returns this (never throws for user-facing errors). `TestNodeResult` (`:302-315`) is the one richer shape.

**Validation.** A single zod schema `nodeSchema` (`:56-87`) + a `parseNodeForm(formData)` adapter (`:91-118`) that trims and coerces every field explicitly — the schema never sees raw `FormData`. First issue only is surfaced: `parsed.error.issues[0]?.message ?? "Invalid node details."` (`:172`, `:202`). Cross-row invariants live in `validateAgainstExisting(data, selfId?)` (`:124-167`), returning `string | null`.

**Secret-field convention (important, reused across the codebase).** Blank `tokenSecret` / `agentToken` on an edit form means "leave unchanged" — the field is *omitted* from the update rather than written (`:212-218`, schema note `:82-86`). The client renders `"•••••• stored — leave blank to keep unchanged"` (`NodeForms.tsx:167`, `:230`). Secrets are never sent back to the browser; the form receives a `hasAgentToken: boolean` presence flag only (`NodeForms.tsx:41-42`).

**`requireAdmin()`** is the first statement of every exported action (`:47, 170, 196, 230, 247, 259, 279, 331, 382`) and its return value supplies `admin.id` for the audit call.

**`audit()`** — in this file it is a **local private helper**, `actions-nodes.ts:29-31`:
```ts
async function audit(userId: string | null, action: string, detail?: string) {
  await db.auditLog.create({ data: { userId, action, detail } });
}
```
Action strings are dotted: `node.create`, `node.update`, `node.enable`/`node.disable`, `node.provisions_enable`, `node.status`, `node.cost.set`/`node.cost.clear`, `node.test.ok`/`node.test.fail`, `node.delete`. **See A5** — this local copy is *not* the shared helper.

**`revalidatePath`.** Every mutation revalidates every surface that renders the row — e.g. `updateNode` does `/admin/nodes`, `/admin/nodes/${id}`, `/admin/infrastructure` (`:223-225`). Create/delete additionally `redirect()` instead of returning (`:192`, `:398`), so `addNode`/`deleteNode` never actually return a success `FormState`.

**Client-side pending/feedback UI (`NodeForms.tsx`) — there is no toast library.** The house pattern is inline status text/banners:

- **Form**: `const [state, action, pending] = useActionState(isEdit ? updateNode : addNode, {})` — `NodeForms.tsx:103`. Same component handles add and edit; edit passes a hidden `id` input (`:111`). Error banner `border-red-500/30 bg-red-500/10 text-red-400` (`:113-117`), success banner emerald (`:118-122`). Submit button `className="btn-primary" disabled={pending}` with `{pending ? "Saving…" : isEdit ? "Save changes" : "Add node"}` (`:257-259`).
- **Inline toggles**: `useTransition` + optimistic-free `start(() => action(...).then(() => {}))` — `EnableToggle` `:343-354`, `StatusSelect` `:412-428`.
- **Save-on-blur numeric field**: `NodeCostInput` `:364-410` — local `value`, `pending`, `err`, transient `saved` flag cleared after 1500 ms; skips the write when unchanged (`:373`).
- **Destructive action**: `DeleteNodeButton` `:430-473` — `window.confirm(...)`, disabled with a `title` reason when blocked, `router.push("/admin/nodes")` on success, inline red error otherwise.
- **Async probe with rich result**: `TestNodeButton` `:266-341`.
- **Field helper** `Field({ label, name, defaultValue, placeholder, type, required, mono, hint })` — `NodeForms.tsx:65-98`, using the global `.label` / `.input` classes.

**CSS vocabulary** (`/opt/nxeon/app/globals.css`): `.card` `:903`, `.card-hover` `:907`, `.section-label` `:1029`, `.btn-primary` `:1041`, `.input` `:1107`, `.label` `:1110`, `.table-shell` `:1124-1135`.

## A5. `requireAdmin` and `audit()`

**`requireAdmin`** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts:229-233`:
```ts
export async function requireAdmin(): Promise<User> {
  const user = await requireUser();
  if (user.role !== "ADMIN") throw new Error("FORBIDDEN");
  return user;
}
```
It builds on `requireUser()` (`auth.ts:223-227`, throws `"UNAUTHORIZED"`), which uses `currentUser()` — i.e. **impersonation-aware**. Related guards in the same file: `requireStaff()` `:240` (uses `realUser()`, ignores impersonation), `assertNotImpersonating()` `:212`, `impersonating()`, `realUser()`.

For **page-level** guards the convention is `requireArea(area)` from `/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:174-180`, which **redirects** (`/login`, `/dashboard`, `/admin`) rather than throwing. `Area` union `rbac.ts:14-38`; `AREA_ROLES` `:40`; `canAccess` `:63`; `isStaff` `:67`; `HREF_AREA` map `:72-159`; `areaForHref` `:161`; `canAccessHref` `:165`.

**`audit()` — there is no single `audit()` export. There are two things:**

1. **The shared writer: `recordAudit(userId: string | null, action: string, detail?: string): Promise<void>`** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/audit.ts:15-22`. It additionally resolves `impersonating()` and appends `actingAdmin=<id>` to `detail` so actions taken during impersonation are attributed to the real admin (`:18-20`). Its own doc comment (`:4-14`) states it was extracted from a private `audit()` in `lib/actions.ts` and that "every other `lib/actions-*.ts` module wrote `db.auditLog.create(...)` ad hoc".

2. **Eight per-file private copies** named `audit()`, all with the same body but **without** the impersonation attribution:
   - `lib/actions-nodes.ts:29`, `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:19`, `lib/actions-billing.ts:8`, `lib/actions-improvements.ts:25`, `lib/actions-staging.ts:14`, `lib/actions-accounting.ts:26`, `lib/actions-work.ts:33`, `lib/actions-company-mail.ts:78`.

   Plus 66 files in `lib/` that call `db.auditLog.create` directly.

For a **new** admin CRUD console, import `recordAudit` from `@/lib/audit` — that is the intended target, even though `actions-nodes.ts` (the reference implementation you asked about) predates it and uses its own copy.

**`AuditLog` model** — `prisma/schema.prisma:1099+`: `{ id, userId?, action, detail?, createdAt, ip?, category? }`. Note `ip` and `category` exist but neither `recordAudit` nor the local `audit()` helpers populate them.

## A5. `requireAdmin` and `audit()`

**`requireAdmin`** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/auth.ts:229-233`:
```ts
export async function requireAdmin(): Promise<User> {
  const user = await requireUser();
  if (user.role !== "ADMIN") throw new Error("FORBIDDEN");
  return user;
}
```
It builds on `requireUser()` (`auth.ts:223-227`, throws `"UNAUTHORIZED"`), which uses `currentUser()` — i.e. **impersonation-aware**. Related guards in the same file: `requireStaff()` `:240` (uses `realUser()`, ignores impersonation), `assertNotImpersonating()` `:212`, `impersonating()`, `realUser()`.

For **page-level** guards the convention is `requireArea(area)` from `/opt/nxeon/lib/rbac.ts:174-180`, which **redirects** (`/login`, `/dashboard`, `/admin`) rather than throwing. `Area` union `rbac.ts:14-38`; `AREA_ROLES` `:40`; `canAccess` `:63`; `isStaff` `:67`; `HREF_AREA` map `:72-159`; `areaForHref` `:161`; `canAccessHref` `:165`.

**`audit()` — there is no single `audit()` export. There are two things:**

1. **The shared writer: `recordAudit(userId: string | null, action: string, detail?: string): Promise<void>`** — `/opt/nxeon/lib/audit.ts:15-22`. It additionally resolves `impersonating()` and appends `actingAdmin=<id>` to `detail` so actions taken during impersonation are attributed to the real admin (`:18-20`). Its own doc comment (`:4-14`) states it was extracted from a private `audit()` in `lib/actions.ts` and that "every other `lib/actions-*.ts` module wrote `db.auditLog.create(...)` ad hoc".

2. **Eight per-file private copies** named `audit()`, all with the same body but **without** the impersonation attribution:
   - `lib/actions-nodes.ts:29`, `lib/actions-admin-billing.ts:19`, `lib/actions-billing.ts:8`, `lib/actions-improvements.ts:25`, `lib/actions-staging.ts:14`, `lib/actions-accounting.ts:26`, `lib/actions-work.ts:33`, `lib/actions-company-mail.ts:78`.

   Plus 66 files in `lib/` that call `db.auditLog.create` directly.

For a **new** admin CRUD console, import `recordAudit` from `@/lib/audit` — that is the intended target, even though `actions-nodes.ts` (the reference implementation you asked about) predates it and uses its own copy.

**`AuditLog` model** — `prisma/schema.prisma:1099+`: `{ id, userId?, action, detail?, createdAt, ip?, category? }`. Note `ip` and `category` exist but neither `recordAudit` nor the local `audit()` helpers populate them.

## B7. `app/sitemap.ts` — hooking in a new large family

`/opt/nxeon/app/sitemap.ts` (279 lines). Single `MetadataRoute.Sitemap` at `/sitemap.xml`. `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` `:9`. `APP_URL` `:7`.

**Structure:**
1. `staticRoutes` array of `{path, priority, freq}` `:14-173` — ~130 hand-listed entries, mapped to entries at `:175-180`.
2. Programmatic families, each an explicit `for` loop pushing entries:
   - `LANDING_SLUGS` → priority 0.7 `:183-190`
   - `REGION_LANDING_SLUGS` → 0.75 `:196-203`
   - `GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS` → 0.6 `:209-216`
   - `GENERAL_LOCATION_SLUGS` → 0.7 `:222-229`
3. DB-driven families, each wrapped in `try/catch` so a missing model can't break the sitemap:
   - Blog posts `:232-251` (defensively feature-detects `db.blogPost` at `:233`)
   - `db.freeMinecraftServer` public+READY → `/servers/{subdomain}` `:260-276`

**How a new "thousands of mod pages" family hooks in:**
1. Export a `MOD_PAGE_SLUGS: string[]` (or an async loader) from a new `lib/marketing/*.ts`.
2. `import` it at the top of `app/sitemap.ts` alongside `:4-5`.
3. Add one `for (const slug of MOD_PAGE_SLUGS) entries.push({ url: \`${APP_URL}/${slug}\`, lastModified: now, changeFrequency: "monthly", priority: 0.5 })` block after `:229`.
4. If slugs come from the DB (`GameMod` rows), copy the `try/catch` idiom at `:260-276` rather than the bare loops.

**Size limits — this is the real risk, and nothing in the repo handles it:**
- **There is no sitemap index.** No `generateSitemaps()` export anywhere, no `app/sitemap/[id]/` route, no `sitemap-index.xml`. `/opt/nxeon/app/robots.ts:18` hardcodes a single `sitemap: ${APP_URL}/sitemap.xml`.
- Current entry count is roughly **130 static + 765 programmatic + blog + public free-MC servers ≈ 900-1000+**, comfortably under the 50,000-URL / 50 MB uncompressed sitemap protocol limit.
- Adding "thousands of mod pages" stays under 50,000 unless the family is very large. `GameMod` is keyed `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` (`prisma/schema.prisma:2932`) with 41 active families — a per-family × per-mod cross-product could plausibly blow past it.
- Because the route is `force-dynamic`, every `/sitemap.xml` request re-runs the whole builder **plus** the two DB queries. At tens of thousands of entries that becomes a real per-request cost with no caching in front of it.
- If you exceed ~10-25k entries, the Next.js-idiomatic fix is `export function generateSitemaps()` in `app/sitemap.ts`, which emits `/sitemap/0.xml`, `/sitemap/1.xml`, … and requires updating `app/robots.ts:18`. **That work does not exist yet.**

## B9. Marketing images

**`next/image` config: there is none.** `/opt/nxeon/next.config.ts` has **no `images` key at all** — no `remotePatterns`, no `domains`, no `formats`, no `deviceSizes`. Every image is either local (`/public/...`) or an `<img>`. A new page family that needs remote images (e.g. Modrinth/CurseForge icon CDNs, `GameMod.iconUrl` at `prisma/schema.prisma:2896`) **will fail** with `next/image` until `images.remotePatterns` is added.

**`next/image` is barely used in marketing** — only 4 files: `components/marketing/ClaudeMark.tsx`, `components/marketing/CompetitorLogo.tsx`, `components/marketing/MarketingFooter.tsx`, `app/(marketing)/about/page.tsx`.

**CSP already allows remote images:** `img-src 'self' data: blob: https:` — `next.config.ts:15`. So raw `<img src="https://…">` works today; only the Next image optimizer is unconfigured.

**`public/` conventions:**
```
public/
  games/           cs2.svg minecraft.svg palworld.png rust.png valheim.png
  games/art/       127 files — <game>_hero.jpg, <game>_logo.png, <game>_poster.jpg
  logos/           competitor/brand logos
  marketing/       about-founders-danang.jpg, auth-wallpaper*.webp, auth-loop.mp4
  blog/  brand/  flags/  nx/  riddle/  dl/
  logo.png  nx-mark.png  favicon.ico  favicon.svg  icon-192.png  icon-512.png  apple-touch-icon.png
```
The `_hero.jpg` / `_logo.png` / `_poster.jpg` triple under `public/games/art/` is the established naming convention for a per-game key-art set — the obvious pattern for a mod-page family to mirror.

**Caching.** `next.config.ts:114-126` explains that this origin has **no CDN**, so specific static paths get `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` via `headers()` at `:127-133`:
```
/logo.png, /nx-mark.png, /games/art/:path*, /logos/:path*
```
**A new image directory gets `max-age=0` by default** — add it to that `headers()` list.

**OG image generation.**
- **One** dynamic OG image: `/opt/nxeon/app/opengraph-image.tsx` — `ImageResponse` from `next/og`, `size = {1200, 630}` `:4`, `contentType = "image/png"` `:5`. Static brand card, Satori-compatible flexbox + inline styles only (`:7`). It is at the **app root**, so it applies to every route that doesn't override it.
- **There is no per-route or dynamic-param OG image.** No `app/(marketing)/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx`, no `app/blog/[slug]/opengraph-image.tsx`. `generateMetadata` in `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx:153-168` sets `openGraph` title/description/url but deliberately no `images`, so every one of the 765 programmatic pages shares the single root card. A per-family OG image would be a new `opengraph-image.tsx` in that family's route dir, modelled on the root one.

=== OsTemplate ===
model OsTemplate {
  id              String        @id @default(cuid())
  slug            String        @unique
  name            String // display name, e.g. "Ubuntu"
  category        ImageCategory @default(PLAIN_OS)
  family          String        @default("linux") // ubuntu | debian | almalinux | rocky | cpanel | ...
  version         String        @default("") // "24.04", "13", ""
  logo            String        @default("") // icon slug for the UI
  vmid            Int // legacy/base template VMID to clone
  baseVmid        Int? // explicit base OS template for panels/apps (falls back to vmid)
  setupScript     String? // shell installed via cloud-init runcmd (panels/apps)
  minRamMB        Int           @default(1024)
  minDiskGB       Int           @default(10)
  licenseRequired Boolean       @default(false) // e.g. cPanel/Plesk need a paid license
  featured        Boolean       @default(false)
  sortOrder       Int           @default(0)
  active          Boolean       @default(true)
  servers         Server[]
}
=== Coupon ===
model Coupon {
  id             String             @id @default(cuid())
  code           String             @unique
  kind           CouponKind
  value          Int
  scope          CouponScope        @default(ANY)
  // Which product family this coupon may be used on at checkout. ANY = no
  // restriction; VPS / GAME limit it to that kind of order.
  serviceKind    CouponServiceKind  @default(ANY)
  // Restrict to ONE specific plan by slug (e.g. "starter"). Null = any plan
  // within `serviceKind`. This is how "one free month on the Starter VPS" is
  // locked to Starter and cannot be spent on a bigger plan.
  planSlug       String?
  // Cap how many months of the term the coupon may discount. 1 = one month only,
  // so a percentage/free coupon cannot be stretched across a 12-month order to
  // give a year free. Null = the whole term.
  maxTermMonths  Int?
  firstTimeOnly  Boolean            @default(false)
  minAmountCents Int?
  maxRedemptions Int?
  timesRedeemed  Int                @default(0)
  expiresAt      DateTime?
  active         Boolean            @default(true)
  note           String?
  createdAt      DateTime           @default(now())
  redemptions    CouponRedemption[]
}
model CouponRedemption {
  id               String    @id @default(cuid())
  couponId         String

=== GamePlan head ===
model GamePlan {
  id           String   @id @default(cuid())
  gameFamily   String // minecraft, valheim, rust, palworld, cs2, terraria, ...
  name         String // e.g. "Minecraft — 4 GB / 20 slots"
  ramMB        Int
  cpuCores     Int      @default(2)
  diskGB       Int
  slots        Int? // player slots (nullable)
  priceCents   Int // retail price the customer pays (per term) — the REGULAR/renewal rate
  /// GRANDFATHER PROGRAM (2026-09-17): mirrors Plan.introPriceCents/introTermMonths

  introPriceCents Int?
  introTermMonths Int?
  termMonths   Int      @default(1)
  basePlanId   String // the VPS Plan used to size/provision the VM
  basePlan     Plan     @relation(fields: [basePlanId], references: [id])
  osTemplateId String? // the game's OsTemplate (image) to deploy

content.text:
# NxLabs feasibility survey — findings ## Headline: this is not greenfield **A working mod catalog + one-click installer already ships in production.** The owner's NxLabs spec largely describes extending it, not building it. Before designing a new schema, read these: | Piece | File | Status | |---|---|---| | Catalog table | `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:2878` `model GameMod` | **Live, 124 rows in prod** | | Per-server install state | `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:2936` `model ServerMod` | Live, 8 INSTALLED / 3 FAILED | | Customer actions | `/opt/nxeon/lib/actions-mods.ts` (261 lines) | Live | | Worker installer | `/opt/nxeon/worker/game-mods.ts` (372 lines) | Live, `ENABLE_REAL_GAMEMODS=1` in `/opt/nxeon/.env:51` | | Job type | `/opt/nxeon/prisma/schema.prisma:88` `GAME_MOD_SYNC` | Live, wired at `worker/index.ts:2253` | | Portal UI | `/opt/nxeon/components/customer/gamepanel/v2/ModsPanel.tsx` | Live, mounted `GamePanelShell.tsx:202` | | Marketing page | `/opt/nxeon/app/(marketing)/game-servers/mods/page.tsx` | Live | | Seeder | `/opt/nxeon/prisma/seed-gamemods.ts` (267 lines) | Live, idempotent upsert on `[gameFamily, slug]` | | Support gate | `/opt/nxeon/lib/mod-install-support.ts` | Live | **Reach today:** 87 of 124 entries are genuinely one-click installable. `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES = {minecraft, rust, valheim}` (`mod-install-support.ts:30`) × `RESOLVABLE_SOURCES = {modrinth, spigotmc, umod, thunderstore}` (`:33`). Blocked: 22 cs2 + 12 palworld (family), 2 github + 1 codefling (source). **Three gaps I verified against the live DB:** 1. **`scripts/verify-gamemods.ts` does not exist.** It's cited in `schema.prisma:2902`, `2924`, `actions-mods.ts:56-58`, and `ModsPanel.tsx:26-32` as the thing that populates the "verified upstream facts." In prod: `verifiedAt=0`, `downloads=0`, `fileBytes=0`, `upstreamOk false=0`, **`iconUrl=0`**. Every honest-data field the panel is designed around is null. NxLabs marketing pages need images — there are zero mod icons. 2. **`/opt/nxeon/components/customer/gamepanel/ModStore.tsx` (521 lines) is dead code** — not imported anywhere. It fabricates star ratings, install counts, versions, and **fake reviews with invented authors** from a slug hash (`:32-56`). The live `ModsPanel.tsx:11-32` documents removing all of it. Worth deleting before it gets revived for NxLabs. 3. `lib/game-mods.ts:1-15` (the marketing `MOD_INFO` copy) still says "Nxeon doesn't curate or auto-install any of this" — stale, contradicts the shipped installer. --- ## 1. Storage — put it on node-4 Surveyed all four hosts read-only. | Node | Pool | Free | Media | RAM free | VMs | |---|---|---|---|---|---| | primary `51.79.162.96` (ns5002569, OVH sgp) | `/` (md3) | **3.7G / 93% full** | — | 8G | 26 | | | `data` (vmdata) | 101G | SSD | | | | | `tank` (vmdata-hdd) | 3.04T | HDD (HGST 4T) | | | | node-2 `178.63.94.114` (Hetzner fsn1) | `rpool` | 359G | SSD | 13G | 19 | | | `tank` | 1.59T | **SSD** (Micron 5200) | | | | node-3 `15.235.145.177` (sgp2) | `data` | 808G | SSD | **2G** | 18 | | node-4 `139.99.125.21` (OVH sgp1) | `data` (vmdata) | 303G | SSD | **44G** | **9** | | | `backup` (vmdata-hdd) | **3.50T** | HDD (HGST 4T) | | | **Recommendation: node-4, a dedicated ZFS dataset on the `backup` pool (3.5T HDD) with the mirror VM's root on `data` (SSD).** Why: most free capacity of any node, most free RAM (44G — ZFS ARC will cache hot mods for free), lowest VM count (9), load average 0.5 on 8 cores, no nginx and nothing on :80/:443 so it's a clean slate, and it's `sgp1` — same region as the primary, so origin-pull latency is low. Sequential file serving is exactly what spinning rust is good at. Caveat: that pool also holds Proxmox `dump` backups, so use a separate dataset and expect I/O contention during backup windows. **Do NOT use the primary.** `/dev/md3` is 49G at **93% used, 3.7G free**, and that's where `/opt/nxeon` lives (`board-uploads` is already 581M, `public/` 72M). This is an incidental risk finding independent of NxLabs — the app host is close to a disk-full outage, and there's precedent: `worker/index.ts:216-225` documents a 2026-09-17 incident where a runaway docker log filled a game server's disk. **Do not use node-3** — 2G RAM free, confirming it's oversold. **No object storage exists.** No S3/R2/B2/minio/bunny SDK in `package.json`; grep hits are marketing copy only (`components/marketing/comparisontemplate/aws-lightsail.ts`, `docs/`). `ROADMAP.md:88` lists Backblaze B2 / OVH Object Storage as an *aspiration* for off-site backups. Current asset strategy is three-way: Postgres bytes (customer UGC), local disk (`/opt/nxeon/board-uploads`, admin-only), or the tenant's own filesystem over SFTP. Adding S3-compatible object storage is a genuine architectural decision, not an existing capability. Note the installer never stages files on our infrastructure anyway — it hands the customer VM a URL and the VM curls it directly (`worker/game-mods.ts:299-310`), so a mirror is a *new* posture, not a drop-in. **Blocker for the creator program:** nginx caps uploads at **20 MB** (`/etc/nginx/sites-available/nxeon:35,62`). Mod jars routinely exceed that. --- ## 2. Schema conventions 189 models, 69 enums. Conventions to match: - **IDs:** `String @id @default(cuid())` — 186 of 189 models. Zero uuid, one autoincrement. - **Timestamps:** `createdAt DateTime @default(now())` near-universal; `updatedAt DateTime @updatedAt` on 53 models (mutable ones only). - **Deletes are HARD.** Only three `archivedAt` columns exist (schema lines 2292, 2345, 2377 — board cards). The catalog idiom is instead a **boolean visibility flag**: `active Boolean @default(true)` (21 models). `GameMod.active` + `GameMod.upstreamOk` (`:2897`, `:2928`) is exactly the "no longer supported" mechanism the owner asked for — `active` for our editorial choice, `upstreamOk` for automated dead-link detection. `getServerMods` filters on both (`actions-mods.ts:109`). - **Enums:** SCREAMING_SNAKE values. But note the mod tables deliberately use **plain `String` with a comment listing values** for `source`, `category`, `status`, `impact`, `serverSide` (`:2883-2887`, `:2942`) — chosen so adding a source doesn't need a migration. Match that for NxLabs. - **Catalog shape** (`OsTemplate`, `GamePlan`, `Coupon`): `slug @unique`, `name`, `category`, `featured Boolean`, `sortOrder Int @default(0)`, `active Boolean @default(true)`. `GameMod` uses `@@unique([gameFamily, slug])` + `@@index([gameFamily, category])` instead of a global unique — correct for a per-family catalog, but **a public URL `/mods/` would need a globally unique slug or a `/mods//` route**. - **Relations:** `Server.userId → User` (`:79-80`), `Server.osTemplateId → OsTemplate` required (`:221-222`), `Server.gamePlanId → GamePlan` nullable (`:228-229`), `Server.nodeId → Node` nullable. `ServerMod` cascades on server delete but **not** on mod delete (`:2939-2941`) — deleting a `GameMod` with installs will FK-error. That's arguably correct; use `active=false`. - **Seeding:** `npx tsx prisma/seed-gamemods.ts`, idempotent upsert. `prisma/catalog.ts` (467 lines) holds OsTemplate/Plan seeds. --- ## 3. "Add to my server" — how it actually works **The pattern is state-driven, not command-driven**, and it's the right one to extend. `installMod` (`actions-mods.ts:183`) writes a desired-state `ServerMod` row (`INSTALLING`/`REMOVING`) and enqueues **one** `GAME_MOD_SYNC` job with no payload; the worker reads the DB and reconciles (`actions-mods.ts:10-21`). Nothing in the job is trustable input. Guardrails already in place: ownership via `ownedServer` (`:23-32`), one-in-flight-job-per-server via `hasInflightJob` (`:34-39`), family match, variant match, pre-flight `installSupport()` refusal so an unrunnable job never consumes the server's one job slot (`:198-203`), and audit rows `gameserver.mod.install` / `.uninstall` (`:222`, `:254`). **Worker mechanics** (`worker/game-mods.ts`): resolve a direct download URL from the source API (`resolveUrl:201-238` — modrinth, spigotmc/spiget, umod, thunderstore), then SSH to the VM as root and have **the VM itself curl the file** into the mod dir (`:299-310`). Deterministic filenames (`nxeon-.jar`, `.cs`, folder `nxeon-`, `planTarget:186-198`) so uninstall is a plain `rm` with no per-install state. Three honest paths (`:16-24`): SANDBOX simulates, real path installs, flag-off marks FAILED with a customer-readable message — it never claims success it didn't achieve. Transport is its own private `withSsh`/`execRemote` (`:336-371`) using `connectionTarget`/`serverRootPassword` from `lib/sftp.ts` — **it does not use `lib/ssh-exec.ts`'s `withServerSsh`**, which is the codebase's other SSH helper. Worth unifying. **Per-family mod paths** (bind mounts confirmed from live prod `OsTemplate.setupScript` rows; `modDirShell` at `worker/game-mods.ts:257-280`): | Family | Bind mount | Mod dir | Wired? | |---|---|---|---| | Minecraft Java | `-v /opt/mc:/data` | `mods/` if variant ∈ {fabric,forge,neoforge,quilt}, else `plugins/`; located by `find`ing `server.properties` (`:263`) | ✅ | | Rust | `-v /opt/rust:/steamcmd/rust` | `find` for `oxide`\|`carbon` → `/plugins` (`:266`) | ✅ | | Valheim | `-v /opt/valheim/config:/config` | hardcoded `/opt/valheim/config/bepinex/plugins` (`:276`) — note the lowercase-`bepinex` bug fix comment at `:267-275` | ✅ | | **Bedrock** | `-v /opt/bedrock:/data` | `behavior_packs/`, `resource_packs/`, **plus** editing `worlds//world_behavior_packs.json` + `world_resource_packs.json` | ❌ not in `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES` | | **Factorio** | `-v /opt/factorio:/factorio` | `/opt/factorio/mods/` + `mod-list.json` | ❌ | I verified the Bedrock layout read-only on the live `upnormal` server (id `cmtsqbpyk0hirhlo7xxf14z1j`, RUNNING): `/opt/bedrock/{behavior_packs,resource_packs,worlds/Bedrock/}` all present, and **both `world_behavior_packs.json` and `world_resource_packs.json` already exist**. Bedrock is the highest-value next family — a JSON-manifest edit, not just a file drop, so it needs a genuinely new adapter kind alongside `jar`/`cs`/`zip`. Its disk is 8.7G at 71% (2.6G free) — mod storage on customer VMs is tight. **Adding a family is deliberately two-part** (`mod-install-support.ts:24-27`): add the dir to `modDirShell` AND the slug to `INSTALLABLE_FAMILIES`. Doing one alone re-creates the exact bug that module exists to prevent. **Restart:** `lib/game-control.ts:95` `GAME_CONTROL: Record` covers **47 families** with `serviceHints` (systemd unit names), `dataRoots`, and RCON config. `worker/index.ts:200` `wrapDockerGameService` rewrites every game's `docker run -d` into a `docker create` + a systemd unit named `serviceHints[0]`, so `systemctl restart ` is uniform across all families. Job type `GAME_POWER` already does start/stop/restart of the game service. **The current mod installer never restarts** — a customer installs a mod and must restart manually. That's a real UX gap for NxLabs. **File manager: yes, mature.** `components/customer/files/FileBrowser.tsx` over `lib/files-adapters.ts` → `lib/actions-files.ts` → `lib/sftp.ts` (primitives `listDir:295`, `writeFileBuffer:501`, `mkdirPath:408`, etc., all SANDBOX-aware). Binary I/O at `app/api/files/[serverId]/route.ts`, 250 MB cap. Uploads land in a fixed `UPLOAD_DIR = /root/nxeon-uploads` (`sftp.ts:120`) with a `validateName`d basename, making path-traversal writes structurally impossible. --- ## 4. Admin conventions `app/admin/` — 1 layout, ~120 pages, ~85 route dirs, `[id]` for details. Nav registry is `/opt/nxeon/lib/admin-groups.ts:47` `ADMIN_NAV` (11 sections, 28 entries, 92 routes); `tabs[0]` is the landing page. Adding a console = an `ADMIN_NAV` entry + an `HREF_AREA` mapping in `lib/rbac.ts:72-159`. **CRUD reference (`lib/actions-nodes.ts` + `components/admin/NodeForms.tsx`):** two action shapes — `(prev: FormState, fd: FormData) => Promise` for forms via `useActionState`, and typed-arg actions for inline row controls via `useTransition`. `type FormState = { error?: string; ok?: boolean }` (`:27`) — never throw for user-facing errors. One zod schema + a `parseNodeForm` adapter so the schema never sees raw FormData. Cross-row invariants in a separate `validateAgainstExisting`. `requireAdmin()` is the first statement of every action. Every mutation `revalidatePath`s every surface rendering the row. **Audit — use `recordAudit` from `/opt/nxeon/lib/audit.ts:15`**, not the local `audit()` in `actions-nodes.ts:29`. The shared one appends `actingAdmin=` during impersonation; eight modules still have private copies that lose that attribution. `actions-mods.ts:222` writes `db.auditLog.create` directly — also should migrate. **UI:** `PageHeader`/`StatCard`/`Badge`/`EmptyState` from `components/ui/primitives.tsx`. **There is no `DataTable`/`AdminTable` and no toast system.** `components/admin/BulkTable.tsx:25` is the nicest table (selection, bulk actions, CSV export) but has only 2 call sites; the dominant idiom is a hand-rolled `` inside `
` — see `app/admin/nodes/page.tsx:249-263`. Feedback is inline banners + `window.confirm`. **Settings/flags:** backed by `model Setting { key @id, value }` (`schema.prisma:1250`). One action, `saveSettings(section, prev, fd)` (`lib/actions-settings.ts:352`), with `SECTION_FIELDS` (`:95-339`) as the server-side allowlist — the client never supplies the key list, and the section is `bind`-ed server-side. A new flag is 3 steps: `SETTINGS_DEFAULTS` in `lib/settings.ts`, a `{key, type:"bool"}` in the `features` section, a `` in `components/admin/settings/FeatureFlagsPanel.tsx`. Read with `getSettingBool()`. --- ## 5. Marketing SEO **Proven pattern: 765 programmatic pages from one route.** `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx` (211 lines) serves four families — `LANDING_SLUGS` (108), `REGION_LANDING_SLUGS` (18), `GAME_LOCATION_SLUGS` (615), `GENERAL_LOCATION_SLUGS` (24) — from `lib/marketing/locationLandings.ts` (89 KB) and `gameLocationLandings.ts` (40 KB). `generateStaticParams` (`:49-53`) is a synchronous concat of the four arrays; `resolve(slug)` (`:112-139`) tries each in a load-bearing order; `generateMetadata` (`:141-169`) returns `{}` for unknown slugs → 404. Note `export const dynamic = "force-dynamic"` (`:44`) — **nothing is prerendered**, so `generateStaticParams` is enumeration-only. **Sitemap hookup** (`app/sitemap.ts`, 279 lines): export a slug array, import it, add one `for` loop pushing `{url, lastModified, changeFrequency, priority}` after line 229. For DB-derived slugs copy the `try/catch` idiom at `:260-276`. **Sitemap is the real risk.** There is **no sitemap index** — no `generateSitemaps()`, no `app/sitemap/[id]/`, and `app/robots.ts:18` hardcodes a single `/sitemap.xml`. Current total is ~900-1000 entries. Thousands of mod pages is survivable (limit is 50,000), but because the route is `force-dynamic` every request re-runs the whole builder plus DB queries with no caching. Past ~10-25k entries you need `generateSitemaps()` + a `robots.ts` change — **that work does not exist**. **JSON-LD** — all in `components/marketing/StructuredData.tsx`: `OrganizationJsonLd:14`, `ProductJsonLd:73`, `ProductOffersJsonLd:114`, `FaqJsonLd:154`, `ArticleJsonLd:171`. - ❌ **No `BreadcrumbJsonLd`** — one inline literal at `app/(marketing)/[slug]/page.tsx:186-200`. Extract it. - ❌ **No `AggregateRating` anywhere.** Two files document the *deliberate* omission (`ToolShell.tsx:38`, `tools/minecraft-server-status/page.tsx:24`): "deliberately NOT paired with aggregateRating/review, since no genuine rating data exists." **The owner's AggregateRating request requires real reviews first** — see §6. - ⚠️ **`SoftwareApplication`** has no shared helper; two inline literals exist. `ToolShell.tsx:44-62` has a private `WebApplicationJsonLd`. - ⚠️ Two different `FaqJsonLd` exports with incompatible props (`StructuredData.tsx:154` takes `items`; `ToolShell.tsx:214` takes `faq`). **Images — a hard blocker.** `next.config.ts` has **no `images` key at all**: no `remotePatterns`, no `domains`. `next/image` with remote mod icons (Modrinth/CurseForge CDNs, `GameMod.iconUrl`) **will throw** until that's added. CSP already permits remote images (`img-src 'self' data: blob: https:`, `next.config.ts:15`), so raw `` works today. There's **no CDN** on this origin (`next.config.ts:114-126`); specific static paths get immutable caching via `headers()` at `:127-133` — **a new image dir defaults to `max-age=0` and must be added to that list.** Convention to mirror: `public/games/art/` with `_hero.jpg` / `_logo.png` / `_poster.jpg` (127 files). OG: one static root card (`app/opengraph-image.tsx`); no per-route OG image exists, so all 765 programmatic pages share it. --- ## 6. Reviews / UGC — essentially nothing exists - `model Review` (`schema.prisma:1271`) is **admin-authored marketing copy with no `userId` at all**. `lib/actions-reviews.ts` is entirely `requireArea("platform")` — there is **no customer-facing write path anywhere**. The only customer touchpoint is an outbound email (`lib/review-request.ts:19`) linking to Trustpilot/Google. - **Homepage badges: real records with a hardcoded fake fallback.** `components/marketing/ReviewBadges.tsx:50-89` queries approved reviews, but `:29-33` `DEMO_BADGES` hardcodes *Trustpilot 4.9/312, HostAdvice 4.8/148, Google 4.9/205* with `href: "#"`, and `:92-94` shows them all-or-nothing when there are no real reviews. `Testimonials.tsx` has the same fallback shape (6 invented personas, with a disclaimer). `CustomerReviews.tsx:31` is honest — returns `null` when empty. - **Does not exist in the schema:** `Rating`, `Vote`/`Like`, `Report`/`Flag`, any `Moderation*` model, blog comments (`BlogPost` has no comments relation), or any mod/product review model. - **No general UGC moderation queue.** The only real customer-content triage is `Feedback` (`schema.prisma:3125`) + `lib/actions-feedback.ts:92` — and it's a status workflow, not approve-before-publish. `KbSuggestion` has a genuine approve/reject but the content is AI-generated. - **Unmoderated today:** `Server.publicDescription` (`schema.prisma:969`) — free customer text published to `/game-servers/directory` with only `.trim().slice(0,500)` (`lib/actions-game-control.ts:1430-1439`). No admin surface lists or takes down listings.
